The theme of this live broadcast is to make traditional Guqia clothing. Before we start today's formal course, let's take a systematic look at how Guqia clothing is made. ## Overview of Traditional Clothing In ancient times, basically all traditional ancient clothes had relatively simple patterns. This simplicity was due to the lack of industrial tools available at that time. The way clothes were worn was also quite simple. In today's live broadcast, we will first learn how to make traditional Greek clothes in a more traditional way. Then we will transition to a more modern, controllable, and easy-to-edit method to create the design shown on our cover. ## Introduction to Marvelous Designer (MD) For those who may not know, Marvelous Designer is a 3D modeling software used for making 3D clothing based on 2D patterns. Our software utilizes a gravity system to simulate 3D effects, allowing users to visualize clothing as it would appear in the real world within a 3D window. If you have any questions, feel free to ask at any time. ## Guqia Clothing Patterns Let's take a look at a post shared by a friend on Douban. The first clothing style we will examine is called "Dorian's Stone." This type of clothing is typically worn by girls and consists of a piece of cloth folded in half, fastened at the waist with a rope. Sometimes, the top can cover the rope, creating a specific style. For example, this plate may have a hole in the back, allowing it to be worn over the rope. If there is no hole, the plate will simply fall down. As a fashion design major, I can relate to many of you. My knowledge in this area was supplemented during my later work experience, as we often did not delve deeply into the clothing of other countries. ## Transition to Greek Fashion Style When transitioning to Greek fashion styles, one variation involves placing the belt on the outside of the folded plate. By adding a belt in the middle, you can see how the style changes slightly, creating some wrinkles in the fabric. The top remains ordinary clothing, but the difference lies in the belt's placement. For example, the style known as "Aionis Hedon" is similar, where the top is folded first, and then the waist is cinched with ropes. In this process, you will notice that the clothing design remains simple, with square panels being a common feature. ## Material Sourcing You can find materials and references online. I recommend using Pinterest (spelled P-I-N-T-E-R-E-S-T) for a wealth of information, although it is primarily in English. For our 3D sewing, multiple options are available in the 3D window. In the MD11 version, you might find that key bindings do not work seamlessly between the 2D and 3D windows. However, in MD12, the software allows for quicker and more efficient operations. ## Clothing Construction Process Now, let's begin the content of today's class. Since we are going to make clothes, we need a virtual model. If you don't have one in your software, you can visit our official mall or website where we constantly update free virtual models. ### Preparing the Virtual Model When working with virtual models, ensure they are positioned in a T-pose for convenience when dressing.
